extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of public water systems and primacy agencies (state regulators) responsible for compliance with 40 CFR Part 141 public notification requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for when, how, and what public water systems (community, non-community, transient) and primacy agencies must notify the public about drinking water violations, monitoring failures, variances/exemptions, and special situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to limit distribution of public notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system may limit distribution of the public notice to only persons served by the portion of the system out of compliance only if permission is granted by the primacy agency in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limiting distribution requires written approval from the primacy agency; otherwise notices must be distributed per the applicable tier requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send copy of notice to primacy agency and Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the notice must also be sent to the primacy agency and the Administrator (as applicable) in accordance with the requirements of § 141.31(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely transmittal of required copies per § 141.31(d) when issuing any public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 1 — Situations requiring Tier 1 public notice
rubrics_metrics.description: List of violation categories and situations requiring a Tier 1 public notice, including: (1) total coliform MCL with fecal coliform or E. coli present or failure to test for fecal coliform/E. coli when required; (2) nitrate/nitrite MCL violations and failure to take confirmation sample within 24 hours; (3) permitted exceedances of nitrate MCL by NCWS where primacy agency allowed; (4) MRDL for chlorine dioxide exceedances in distribution system following an entrance exceedance or failure to take required distribution samples; (5–6) turbidity and certain SWTR/IESWTR/LT1ESWTR treatment technique exceedances when primacy agency determines Tier 1 required or consultation not completed within 24 hours; (7) waterborne disease outbreak or other waterborne emergency; (8) detection of E. coli, enterococci, or coliphage in source water as specified; (9) other situations with significant potential for serious short-term health effects as determined by primacy agency; (10) exceedance of lead action level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A identifies tier assignments for each specific violation or situation. Tier 1 is for situations with significant, short-term health risks and often triggers the fastest notification timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 1 — Timing and additional steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems must: (1) provide notice as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after learning of the violation/situation; (2) initiate consultation with the primacy agency as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours; and (3) comply with any additional public notification requirements determined through consultation (timing, form, manner, frequency, content, repeat notices, and other actions to reach all persons served).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation outcomes may impose additional requirements; follow-up actions and repeat notices may be required. Time limits are strict (24 hours) for initial notice and consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 1 — Form and manner (delivery methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tier 1 public notice must be provided within 24 hours in a form and manner reasonably calculated to reach all persons served, designed to reach residential, transient, and non-transient users. Minimum delivery methods include: (1) appropriate broadcast media (radio/TV); (2) posting in conspicuous locations throughout the area served; (3) hand delivery to persons served; or (4) another delivery method approved in writing by the primacy agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose delivery methods appropriate to the population served; primacy agency may approve alternate methods in writing. Use enough methods to reach all affected groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 2 — Situations requiring Tier 2 public notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations and situations requiring Tier 2 notice include: (1) all MCL, MRDL, and treatment technique violations except where Tier 1 is required or primacy agency determines Tier 1; (2) certain monitoring and testing procedure violations where primacy agency determines Tier 2 is warranted (considering health impacts and persistence); (3) failure to comply with terms of any variance or exemption; (4) failure to take corrective action or maintain required 4-log virus treatment under § 141.403(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A cross-references specific violations to Tier 2. Primacy agency judgment may move a violation between tiers based on health risk and persistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 2 — Timing, posting duration, and repeat frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial Tier 2 notice must be provided as soon as practical but no later than 30 days after system learns of the violation. If posted, notice must remain while the violation persists but no less than seven days. Primacy agency may, in appropriate circumstances, allow additional time for the initial notice up to three months in writing but not for unresolved violations or across-the-board extensions. The system must repeat the notice every three months while the violation persists unless primacy agency determines otherwise; repeat notices must be at least annually; reductions in repeat frequency must be in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume blanket extensions or reduced repeat frequency — primacy agency must authorize any exception in writing. Maintain documentation of extensions or modified frequencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 2 — Turbidity consultation and contingency
rubrics_metrics.description: For specified turbidity violations, public water systems must consult with the primacy agency as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours to determine whether a Tier 1 notice is required. If consultation does not occur within 24 hours, the system must distribute a Tier 1 notice within the next 24 hours (i.e., no later than 48 hours after learning of the violation). Consultation is required for turbidity MCL violations under § 141.13(b) and for certain SWTR/IESWTR/LT1ESWTR single exceedance turbidity TT violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If primacy agency cannot be reached within 24 hours, default to issuing Tier 1 notice within 48 hours to protect public health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 2 — Form and manner for community systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless directed otherwise in writing by the primacy agency, community water systems must provide Tier 2 notice by: (i) mail or other direct delivery to each customer receiving a bill and to other service connections to which water is delivered; and (ii) any other method reasonably calculated to reach other persons regularly served who would not be reached by the delivery in (i) (examples: publication in local newspaper; delivery of multiple copies for distribution by customers who provide water to others; posting in public places or on the Internet; delivery to community organizations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and use supplemental methods to reach renters, students, institutional residents, and others who may not receive bills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 2 — Form and manner for non-community systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless directed otherwise in writing by the primacy agency, non-community water systems must provide Tier 2 notice by: (i) posting the notice in conspicuous locations throughout the distribution system frequented by persons served, or by mail/direct delivery to each customer/service connection (where known); and (ii) any other method reasonably calculated to reach other persons served who would not normally be reached by the posting (examples: publication in local newspaper/newsletter; e-mail to employees or students; delivery of multiple copies in central locations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post in locations routinely visited by the served population and supplement with other outreach as needed to reach all affected people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 3 — Situations requiring Tier 3 public notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Tier 3 notice is required for: (1) monitoring violations under 40 CFR part 141 except where Tier 1 or Tier 2 applies; (2) failure to comply with a testing procedure in part 141 except where Tier 1 or Tier 2 applies; (3) operation under a variance or exemption; (4) availability of unregulated contaminant monitoring results; (5) exceedance of fluoride SMCL; (6) reporting and recordkeeping violations under subpart Y, among others indicated in Appendix A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tier 3 is for violations/situations with primarily informational or lower short-term health risk; Appendix A maps specific items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 3 — Timing and repeat requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems must provide Tier 3 initial notice not later than one year after learning of the violation/situation or beginning operation under a variance/exemption. The system must repeat the notice annually while the situation persists. If posted, the notice must remain while the situation persists but no less than seven days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reporting or a single CCR can substitute provided timing and content requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 3 — Annual report/CCR option
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of individual Tier 3 notices, a public water system may use an annual report detailing all violations/situations during the previous 12 months, as long as the timing requirements are met. For community systems, the Consumer Confidence Report (CCR) may be used as vehicle for initial Tier 3 notice and repeats if provided within 12 months, follows content requirements of § 141.205, and is distributed following § 141.204(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using CCR or annual report, ensure the Tier 3 notice content and distribution timing exactly match regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tier 3 — Form and manner for community and non-community systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Tier 3 form/manner requirements are analogous to Tier 2: community systems should use mail/direct delivery to bill-paying customers and other methods to reach those not reached by bills; non-community systems should post in conspicuous locations or use mail/direct delivery where known and provide other methods to reach those who may not see postings (publication, e-mail, multiple copies in central locations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select methods reasonable to reach persons served within the one-year timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice content elements (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each public notice for NPDWR violations or other situations requiring notice must include: (1) a description of the violation/situation including contaminant(s) and contaminant levels (if applicable); (2) when the violation/situation occurred; (3) any potential adverse health effects including required standard language; (4) the population at risk including particularly vulnerable subpopulations; (5) whether alternative water supplies should be used; (6) what actions consumers should take, including when to seek medical help, if known; (7) what the system is doing to correct the violation/situation; (8) when the system expects to return to compliance or resolve the situation; (9) name, business address, and phone number of the system owner/operator/designee for more information; (10) a statement encouraging distribution of the notice to others served, using standard language where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All ten elements must be present unless a specific exception or alternate wording is authorized; include contaminant levels and clear health guidance when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content for variance/exemption notices
rubrics_metrics.description: If a system is operating under a variance or exemption, the public notice must contain: (i) an explanation of the reasons for the variance/exemption; (ii) the date issued; (iii) a brief status report on steps the system is taking to install treatment, find alternative sources, or otherwise comply with terms/schedules; and (iv) notice of any opportunity for public input in the review. If system violates the conditions of a variance/exemption, the notice must contain the ten elements listed for NPDWR violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include status updates and public engagement opportunities; violation of conditions triggers full content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation requirements (readability and visibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each public notice must be displayed conspicuously when printed/posted; must not contain overly technical language or very small print; must not be formatted in a way that defeats the purpose of the notice; and must not contain language that nullifies the purpose of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain language, legible fonts/sizes, and formats that maximize comprehension and visibility for the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems serving a large proportion of non-English speaking consumers (as determined by primacy agency), the notice must contain information in the appropriate language(s) regarding the importance of the notice or contain a telephone number/address where persons may obtain a translated copy or request assistance. Where primacy agency has not made such a determination, the system must include similar information where appropriate to reach a large proportion of non-English speaking persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess population language needs (or follow primacy agency determinations) and provide translations or accessible means to obtain translated notices; include contact info for translation requests when full translated text is not included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard language requirements (health effects, monitoring violations, distribution encouragement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must include: (1) standard health effects language for MCL/MRDL/treatment technique violations and violations of variance/exemption conditions as specified in appendix B; (2) specified monitoring/testing procedure violation language (with blanks to fill in compliance period and contaminants); (3) standard distribution encouragement language urging recipients to share the notice with others who drink the water, with examples of how to share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exact appendix B health-effect wording for the relevant violation; use provided monitoring violation template language verbatim with appropriate insertions; include standard 'please share' language where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to new billing units or new customers
rubrics_metrics.description: Community water systems must give a copy of the most recent public notice for any continuing violation, variance/exemption, or other ongoing situation requiring notice to all new billing units or new customers prior to or at the time service begins. Non-community systems must continuously post the public notice in conspicuous locations to inform new consumers while the situation persists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure onboarding processes include delivery of current notices to new customers and that posted notices remain current and visible for new consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special notice for availability of unregulated contaminant monitoring results
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators required to monitor under § 141.40 must notify persons served of availability of sampling results no later than 12 months after results are known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form and manner must follow Tier 3 notice requirements (§§141.204(c), (d)(1), and (d)(3)). The notice must identify a person and provide a telephone number for information on results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special notice for fluoride SMCL exceedance — timing, repeat, recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Community systems exceeding fluoride SMCL (2 mg/L) but not MCL (4 mg/L) must provide the special notice as soon as practical but no later than 12 months after learning of exceedance; send a copy to new billing units/customers at service start and to the State public health officer. The notice must be repeated at least annually while SMCL is exceeded; if posted must remain while exceeded but not less than seven days. Primacy agency may require initial notice sooner or more frequent repeats on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Tier 3 form/manner requirements; be prepared to act more quickly if primacy agency requires it; document distribution to new customers and the State public health officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special fluoride notice mandatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: The fluoride special notice must contain specified language (including fill-in blanks) advising about cosmetic dental problems (dental fluorosis) affecting children under nine, the measured fluoride concentration, advice that children under nine should be provided alternative water or treated water to avoid staining/pitting, contact information for system, and optional information about home treatment units and NSF International contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact mandated wording and fill in the system name, measured value, and contact information; do not paraphrase or omit required health warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special notice for nitrate exceedances by NCWS with primacy permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-community water systems granted permission by the primacy agency under § 141.11(d) to exceed the nitrate MCL must provide notice to persons served according to Tier 1 requirements (§141.202(a) and (b)). Form/manner: continuous posting that nitrate levels exceed 10 mg/L and potential health effects, following Tier 1 delivery requirements and §141.205 content requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When operating under written permission to exceed nitrate MCL, comply with Tier 1 urgency and content; ensure continuous conspicuous posting for as long as permitted exceedance exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy agency may give notice on behalf of system
rubrics_metrics.description: The primacy agency may give the notice required by this subpart on behalf of the owner/operator if the primacy agency complies with the subpart's requirements. The owner/operator remains responsible for ensuring the subpart's requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If primacy agency issues the notice, the system must still ensure content, timing, and distribution obligations are fulfilled and retain documentation of compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special notice for repeated failure to monitor source water for Cryptosporidium
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems required to monitor under § 141.701 must notify persons served that monitoring has not been completed as specified no later than 30 days after failing to collect any 3 months of required monitoring. The notice must be repeated per § 141.203(b) (Tier 2 repeat schedule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Tier 2 form/manner and presentation requirements; include required mandatory language template and contact information; not required if complying with a State-approved schedule to address the violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special notice for failure to determine Cryptosporidium bin classification or mean level
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems required to determine bin classification under § 141.710 or mean Cryptosporidium level under § 141.712 must notify persons served that the determination has not been made as required no later than 30 days after failing to report the determination. The notice must be repeated per § 141.203(b). The notice is not required if the system is complying with a State-approved schedule to address the violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mandatory template language provided in § 141.211(d)(2) and include a description of corrective actions and expected return to compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Cryptosporidium notice required content and corrective action description
rubrics_metrics.description: Each special Cryptosporidium notice must use the specified language templates (for repeated failure to conduct monitoring and for failure to determine bin classification/mean level) and must also include a description of what the system is doing to correct the violation and when it expects to return to compliance or resolve the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the exact template wording with appropriate dates, treatment plant name, contact name/phone, and include corrective action status and anticipated compliance timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A — mapping of specific contaminants/violations to tiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix A lists specific NPDWR contaminants, monitoring/testing violations, and other situations and identifies the tier of public notice required for each (microbiological contaminants, IOCs, SOCs, VOCs, radioactive contaminants, DBPs, PFAS entries, etc.), with citations to the specific regulatory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult Appendix A to determine the tier for a specific contaminant or violation and follow the tier-specific timing, form, and content rules. Appendix A contains extensive, itemized mappings and citations; use it to classify the required notice level.
